title: Comparison pullbacks of injective left-module sheaves are acyclic for arbitrary rings
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\Lambda$ a discrete associative unital ring, not assumed commutative, in the coefficient universe. Use the small étale and pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] in a common larger universe in which their underlying categories are small. A $\Lambda$-module sheaf means a sheaf of left $\Lambda$-modules; equivalently it is a sheaf of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over the constant sheaf of rings, the sheafification of the constant ring presheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $
u_X:X_{\mathrm{proét}}	o X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ be the comparison geometric morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. On module sheaves, $
u_X^*$ applies its set inverse image to addition, zero, negation and each scalar endomorphism of the underlying abelian sheaf; $
u_{X,*}$ is restriction to the étale subsite, with its induced scalar actions. Compute $R^q
u_{X,*}$ by injective resolutions in these module categories [def-sp-left-exact-additive, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Then for every injective left $\Lambda$-module sheaf $I$ on $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ and every integer $q>0$,
$$
R^q
u_{X,*}(
u_X^*I)=0.
$$
No affineness, quasi-compactness, torsion or finite-ring hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Work in the common larger universe already fixed in the statement. On each of the two small sites take the constant sheaf of associative unital rings associated to $\Lambda$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] their categories of left-module sheaves are Grothendieck abelian, without any commutativity assumption. By [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] both have enough injectives. Thus the module injective resolutions used below exist. Put $F=I_{ab}$ and $M=\nu_X^*I$. By the explicit construction in the statement, $M_{ab}=\nu_X^{-1}F$: forgetting scalar endomorphisms leaves exactly the inverse-image addition, zero and negation of the abelian sheaf.

source.place: Tag 079Q (remark-existence-D), module categories on a ringed site; the action construction is the one explicitly fixed in the item statement

proof.text: Let $v:W\to X$ be any object of $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$, with no affineness assumption. The inclusion defining [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] also regards $W$ as an object of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$. On abelian sheaves, étale inverse image along $v$ is restriction, by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction]; the first sentence of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives] identifies $W_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with the slice over $W$. The pro-étale inverse image is the slice restriction of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], as follows directly from the base-change direct image in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Indeed a map $\alpha:G|_W\to H$ corresponds to $\beta:G\to v_*H$ given on $V$ by $G(V)\to G(V\times_XW)\xrightarrow{\alpha}H(V\times_XW\to W)$; conversely restrict $\beta_T$ along the graph $T\to T\times_XW$ for each $T\to W$. Naturality and the identity of the first projection composed with this graph show the two constructions are inverse. Thus restriction is the left adjoint to the specified direct image, hence the specified inverse image. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] to the abelian sheaf $F$ and this $v$. It gives $\nu_W^{-1}(F|_W)\cong(\nu_X^{-1}F)|_W=M_{ab}|_W$. This uses only the abelian inverse-image square and the slice identification; it invokes no finite-ring assertion about module pullback or module restriction.

source.place: Tag 099V (lemma-relative-comparison), localization to étale objects; slice restrictions as in sites-cohomology.tex Tag 03F3 (lemma-cohomology-of-open)

proof.text: For $q>0$ and the same étale object $W$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison] on $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ identifies $H^q(W,F)$ with $R^q\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod}}(W,-)(I)$. The latter is zero by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-injective-vanishing], since $I$ is injective in the module category and evaluation to abelian groups is additive and left exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-over-object-localization] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open], $H^q(W,F)$ is also $H^q(W_{\mathrm{ét}},F|_W)$. Thus $H^q(W_{\mathrm{ét}},F|_W)=0$. In particular the argument has not asserted that $F$ itself is an injective abelian sheaf.

source.place: Tags 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree) and 03F3 (lemma-cohomology-of-open); derived.tex Tag 015B (lemma-higher-derived-functors), injective vanishing

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-abelian-etale-proetale-cohomology-comparison] to the scheme $W$ and the abelian sheaf $F|_W$. Together with steps 2 and 3 this gives $H^q(W_{\mathrm{proét}},M_{ab}|_W)=0$ for every étale $W\to X$ and $q>0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-over-object-localization], using the pro-étale slice identification from step 2, this is $H^q(W,M_{ab})=0$ computed on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison] now on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with its constant ring sheaf: $R^q\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod}}(W,-)(M)\cong H^q(W,M_{ab})=0$. The enough-injectives hypothesis is supplied by step 1. The comparison theorem has no torsion, finiteness, fixed ring or commutativity hypothesis, so it applies to this underlying abelian sheaf for the given arbitrary $\Lambda$.

Choose a module injective resolution $M	o J^ ullet$ on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. The module direct image $
u_{X,*}$ is additive because its addition and zero maps are evaluated sectionwise, and it preserves kernels because both restriction and module-sheaf kernels are sectionwise [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Thus it is left exact in the sense of [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. By the resolution formula in [def-sp-left-exact-additive] and step 4, the complex of abelian groups $J^ ullet(W)$ is exact at each degree $q>0$ for every étale object $W	o X$. By the restriction definition of $
u_{X,*}$ in the statement and [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], $(
u_{X,*}J^ ullet)(W)=J^ ullet(W)$ with the same differentials. Hence in positive degrees the sectionwise image equals the sectionwise kernel on every object of $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$. Kernels of module sheaves are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; therefore a complex exact on every object is exact as a complex of module sheaves. Its degree-$q$ cohomology sheaf, which by definition is $R^q
u_{X,*}(M)$, is zero. Substituting $M=
u_X^*I$ proves the assertion.

lean.note: Existing generic coefficient theorem, read in the source and in current server source via scompile.py --source. Specialize its ambient A to ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ with Λ : Type (u + 1) and [Ring Λ]. Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.AB supplies IsGrothendieckAbelian.{u + 1} with no commutativity or finiteness assumption; all required instances and the exact specialization were checked with scompile.py. Sheaf-valued left modules are the first, fixed-scalar encoding explicitly allowed in the node. The upstream comparison functors are restriction and canonical left Kan extension followed by sheafification, the same constructions as the recorded geometric comparison. Functor.rightAcyclic unfolds to every positive rightDerived degree. The stored signature is verbatim; A and its categorical instances are the surrounding variables in that source module. No duplicate module is delivered.
